Lower bound basis: The ultimate strength is the maximum stress, so it is at least the yield and break stress; a printed part is strongest in XY, so a value in any direction bounds the XY one.

Related properties: Elongation at break; Elongation at yield
Lower bound properties: Elongation at break; Elongation at yield; Tensile strain at strength
Lower bound basis: A bar breaks after it yields and after it reaches its maximum stress; XY strain at break is at least the strain in any other direction. A conditioned value bounds nothing: absorbed water plasticises a nylon and raises its strain, so it can exceed the dry headline.
Hint: how far it stretches before it snaps; not the same as springing back or toughness
